workflowArticle.title: Use file age to investigate forgotten space on a Mac
workflowArticle.primaryIntent: Interpret a size-and-age storage map without treating old files as disposable; decide when a one-time map is enough and when recurring investigation is needed.
workflowArticle.descriptionDirection: Large, old folders are candidates for investigation, not automatic deletion. Explain Klarity's documented age map and allocated-space caveats, then ownership, backup and rebuild-cost checks.
sections: Start with the largest old area, not a clean-everything button
Read modified age, allocated size and cloud placeholders as different signals
Inspect ownership, project dependencies and backup status before any removal
Separate one-time storage mapping from recurring-growth investigation
Choose the map, manual Finder review or broader maintenance based on the job
distinctiveEvidence: K06 explicit no deletion instructions while documentation conflict remains
workflowArticle.visualPlan: Accessible official treemap directly after lead; current Space example-data preview later, with required caption. Neither demonstrates measured recovery.
workflowArticle.interactionPass: Hand off a local decision checklist: known owner, backed up, original versus rebuildable, available offline, rebuild/download cost. Unknown answers mean defer, not permission. No filesystem API, uploads or deletion.
workflowArticle.linkCaveat: Proposed targets only, not validated live routes. Link a relevant unit/cleanup-planning tool only if implemented and independently tested.
